Experiment 8 results: how narrow a linear feature can Sentinel-1 show?

What we found

Width mattered less than expected for Sentinel-1

  • 803 road, track, ditch and field-edge segments in 22 Capella scenes were measured at sub-meter detail.
  • A multi-date Sentinel-1 mean showed half of them at about 5.5 m width (2.8 to 15.7 m); a single date needed about 15 m. Neither reached 90% at any width.
  • Ditches gave the cleanest curve: 50% at 3.2 m. Hedgerows gave no usable result.
  • The test knows where each line is and averages along 200 m, so it is an upper bound for per-pixel boundary mapping.

Status: done (2026-10-28). CPU only.

Result

Width alone doesn't decide whether Sentinel-1 shows a linear feature. Each test segment is a 200 m stretch of feature that Capella shows clearly. With a multi-date mean of Sentinel-1 VV and VH, the pre-set test detected about half of these segments at almost any width: 45% of features 2–3 m wide, 52% at 5–8 m and 63% at 12–20 m. A single date detected fewer, rising from 27% at 2–3 m to 60% at 12–20 m. Neither curve reaches 90% within the measured range of 1 to 40 m.

Sentinel-1 product Segments Detected Width at 50% detection Width at 90% detection
Multi-date mean, VV or VH 803 51% 5.5 m (2.8–15.7) beyond 40 m
Single date, VV or VH 803 38% 14.9 m (9.0 to beyond 40) beyond 40 m
Multi-date mean, VV only 803 39% 15.9 m (8.9 to beyond 40) beyond 40 m
Multi-date mean, VH only 803 36% 24.9 m (12.1 to beyond 40) beyond 40 m
Reference: Capella blurred to 20 m 803 74% 3.0 m (2.6–3.5) 9.2 m (7.3–12.5)

Widths come from a logistic curve whose floor is the measured false-alarm rate (5.0–5.6%). Ranges in parentheses are 95% intervals from 1,000 bootstrap draws of scenes (500 for the reference).

The reference row explains the gap. The same test, applied to Capella's own profile after blurring it to about the 20 m Sentinel-1 resolution, detects 92% of features 8–12 m wide and all features wider than 20 m. Resolution alone would therefore let a 10 m sensor show most features wider than about 9 m. Sentinel-1 misses many of them because its C-band VV and VH contrast differs from Capella's X-band HH contrast. Fields on either side often look the same at C-band, a road or ditch gives little contrast, and speckle hides weak contrast.

Type Segments (scenes) Median width Detected Width at 50% Width at 90%

Hedgerows and tree lines 3 (2) 4.2 m 0 of 3 too few too few

Ditches and canals are the one type with a clear width curve. Dark ditches (82 segments) reach 50% at 4.4 m (2.0–5.9) and 90% at 11.4 m (8.1–21.0) in the multi-date mean. Single dates give 7.8 m and beyond 40 m for all ditches. Roads, tracks and field-edge strips stay near 45–60% across widths. For roads the single-date curve rises from 25% at 2–3 m to about 50% above 12 m, while the multi-date mean sits near 50% throughout. Hedgerows didn't yield a usable sample (see the limits).

Contrast, brightness, polarization and direction

  • Capella contrast barely matters. In a fit with both log width and |contrast|, a 1 dB rise in X-band contrast raises the odds of detection by only 2% (multi-date) or 0.5% (single date). The width at 50% moves from 6.4 m at 2 dB contrast to 3.9 m at 12 dB. A bright 3 m road and a dark 3 m ditch differ less at C-band than their X-band contrast suggests. The width-by-contrast grid shows no consistent gradient along the contrast axis.
  • Bright features do better on single dates. Features that are bright on Capella reach 50% at 6.2 m (4.0–19.4) on a single date, dark ones at 26 m. In the multi-date mean the difference shrinks (3.9 m against 6.6 m).
  • Two polarizations beat one. VV alone or VH alone detects 36–39% in the multi-date mean. Allowing either one, with a stricter threshold that keeps the false-alarm rate at 5.4%, detects 51%.
  • Direction relative to the flight path makes little difference. Features within 30° of the flight direction and features more than 60° from it reach 50% at 4.4 m and 7.0 m in the multi-date mean, with overlapping intervals.
  • The sign often agrees. Among detected segments, the Sentinel-1 contrast has the same sign as Capella's in 74% of VV detections and 66–69% of VH detections.

What "detected" means here

The test asks whether Sentinel-1 shows any contrast at a known 200 m line, averaged along the whole line, compared with parallel lines 40–75 m away. That is a lenient test. It knows where to look, and averaging along 20 pixels removes most speckle. A field-boundary mapper sees one pixel at a time and doesn't know the line's position, so it needs more contrast. Read these curves as an upper bound on what a 10 m map can recover.

The test also responds to anything along the line, not only to the measured feature. A 2 m track usually runs with a verge, a crop change or a ditch beside it. The spot-check panels show cases where Sentinel-1 gives a broad 1 dB step across a narrow, bright Capella road. That is why narrow features score near 45% in the multi-date mean: often the corridor is detected, not the track. This matters less for field-boundary mapping, where the corridor is the boundary, but it means the curve doesn't measure a resolution limit.

Method

Scenes. From experiment 6's 190 Capella items over cropland with a matched Sentinel-1 pass, one item per site (finest resolution, then the closest pass in time). A 4 km window went where rural OSM lines were densest. That gave 30 scenes in 18 countries after the cap of 4 per country (scenes_selected.csv, windows.geojson). Eight scenes failed the alignment check below. The headline uses the other 22 scenes in 14 countries: Poland, Spain, the United States, Germany, Myanmar, the United Kingdom, Austria, Australia, Taiwan, the Netherlands, Russia, Georgia, Italy and Moldova. All but two Capella items are HH.

Lines. OpenStreetMap lines via Overture Maps (release 2026-10-21.0), because the public Overpass servers were at capacity. Roads, tracks and paths, ditches, drains and canals, hedges, tree rows and outlines of farmland, meadow, orchard and vineyard. A field-edge strip is a land-use outline with no other mapped line within 30 m. Lines were cut into 200 m segments. Segments with a parallel mapped line within 30 m, or with crossings along more than 40% of their length, were dropped.

Width on Capella. Capella GEO amplitude averaged to 1 m. Perpendicular profiles every 1 m along each segment, averaged in ten 20 m blocks. The blocks were aligned to each other by up to ±4 m and averaged again. Width is the full width at half contrast against the mean of the two background levels. A segment counts as a clear feature only with Capella matched-null |z| ≥ 4, |contrast| ≥ 1 dB, similar backgrounds on both sides (not a step between two fields), and the extremum in at least 6 of 10 blocks. Of 11,700 segments in the 22 scenes, 4,900 had parallel neighbors, 1,100 too many crossings and 1,100 no Capella data, and 3,400 showed no clear feature. 803 passed.

Sentinel-1. Planetary Computer RTC (terrain-corrected gamma0, 10 m, VV and VH). Single date: the pass nearest Capella, a median 0.6 days away (all within 10 days). Multi-date mean: every pass from that track within ±30 days, typically 4–5 dates and up to 10. No speckle filter.

Detection rule (set before measuring). At the Capella-measured center, contrast is the mean of the center window, |d| ≤ max(5 m, width / 2), against the two 15 m flanks. The null is the same statistic on 16 parallel lines placed so that their windows stay 10 m clear of the feature. Detected when |z| > 2 in one polarization, or > 2.24 in VV or in VH for the headline. The false-alarm rate comes from applying the rule to each null line against the other 15.

Alignment. Capella GEO sat up to 270 m from its true position (site 299, hilly Austria) and 10–40 m off elsewhere. A coarse shift comes from cross-correlating Capella at 10 m with the multi-date VV over ±1.5 km. Correlation leans on trees and buildings, whose layover differs between X-band and C-band. A second step therefore fits the Capella centers of roads, tracks and ditches to the OSM lines and shifts Capella by that offset (median residual scatter 4.9 m). Scenes with fewer than 8 such ground features couldn't be checked and leave the headline.

Changes to the plan. DESIGN.md records three amendments and one code fix, all made before any Sentinel-1 result was looked at. They cover the Overture source and rural window placement, the two-step alignment and the ground-feature shift. The code fix repaired a block-alignment bug that had shifted every center by 4 m. One check came after seeing results. The pre-set contrast mixes a linear mean (center) with a dB mean (flanks), which can turn a plain step between two fields into a positive contrast. rescore.py recomputes everything with all three windows averaged in dB. Detection stayed at 51% (multi-date) and 38–39% (single date), and the width at 50% stayed at 5.5 m (2.9–13.8) and 14.8 m (width_table_db.csv, figures/*_db.png). Including the 8 unchecked scenes (868 segments) gives 5.3 m and 13.5 m.

Limits

  • OSM position. OSM lines can be off by several meters, and some mapped features don't exist on the ground. The ±15 m search and the clear-feature rule remove those, so the sample favors well-mapped, high-contrast features. After alignment, Capella centers scatter 2–9 m around the OSM lines per scene. Residual misregistration of a few meters weakens the center window for narrow features at 10 m pixels.
  • HH against VV. 20 of the 22 Capella scenes are HH, at X-band. Sentinel-1 is VV and VH at C-band. The contrast that makes a feature clear on Capella need not exist at C-band, which the gap to the blurred-Capella reference shows.
  • Look direction and incidence. The flight direction comes from an orbit approximation. X-band layover shifts tall features toward the sensor, so the Capella center of a hedge or tree line isn't where Sentinel-1 sees it. That helps explain why tree lines failed. Only 23 tree lines passed the Capella checks, mostly in UK site 239. That scene had too few ground features to check, so 3 remain in the headline. This experiment says nothing reliable about hedgerows.
  • Speckle. Single dates detect 10–20 points less than the multi-date mean at most widths. Five dates aren't a full seasonal composite either.
  • Width resolution. Capella Stripmap and Sliding Spotlight resolve about 1 m. Only 11 features measured under 2 m, so the curve below 2 m isn't measured.
  • Widest features. Only 34 segments are wider than 20 m. The dip at 20–40 m rests on few segments, and some wide features are canals or roads whose flanks reach other structures.
  • Lenient test. Known position and 200 m averaging make detection easier than per-pixel mapping.

Spot check

spotcheck/ holds 60 panels from the headline scenes, stratified by type, width class and multi-date outcome (30 detected, 30 not). Each shows Capella at 1 m (purple outline, the truth), Sentinel-1 VV single date, VV and VH multi-date means (no outline; no detector output is drawn) and the across-line profiles. spotcheck.csv lists them with an empty verdict column.

Files

Scripts: select_scenes.py, measure.py, analyze.py (set EXP8_VARIANT=db for the dB variant), rescore.py, blur_reference.py, figure_reference.py, spotcheck.py. Tables: scenes_selected.csv, scene_meta.csv, segments_all.csv, segment_status.csv, curve_bins.csv, width_table.csv, width_contrast_grid.csv, summary.json, blur_reference.csv, plus _db versions. Figures in figures/. Data in data/ (0.7 GB, gitignored). Downloads were about 2.9 GB per full run (Capella tiles 2.4 GB, Sentinel-1 0.5 GB). Pilots and three reruns bring the total to about 10 GB, plus unmetered Overture range reads.
